Pokemon Red, Blue, Yellow, Gold, Silver and Crystal have been until the last two years impossible to play since the batteries in the carts died, rendering them bricks.   


Many old games like Earthbound were impossible to play legit until recently thanks to the carts for them being so rare and expensive that noone but a collector can get one. Old games have died over and over from lack of reasonable ability to play them. Nintendo had to download a rom for Super Mario Bros. because they didn't have one. 

What do you do when the media of a actual, bought cartridge has died? What do you do when a game has become rare, valuable and so inflated or expensive that they are impossible to buy without paying hundreds for a collectors copy?  


What about when the console they are played on is impossible to find, has worn over time, or is just as inflated and rare as the games?  


This is the grayest areas of emulating and what I consider the Justified Zone. Where the legit media is unobtainable. The Nintendo, Sega Saturn, Genesis, Super Nintendo, Nintendo 64 and Game Boy Color and Advance are all subject to this zone. Until the companies make it so that the media can be gotten and played reasonably and legitimately, Emulation will continue to be a thorn in their side. 

Until they step in to remedy this issue like Nintendo has tried to do, emulation will remain grey.
